newsitem.title: USA: CBOT old crop soymeal, soybeans turn up on exports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT old crop soymeal, soybeans turn up on exports.

text.p: CBOT old crop soymeal and soybean futures turned higher in fast dealings after USDA put weekly soybean export inspections above trade expectations, pit sources said.
USDA said 12.536 million bushels of soybeans were inspected for export, above trade expectations for six million to 10 million bushels.
The May soymeal contract set a contract high at $308.50 per ton, topping the previous high of $305.40 set on Friday and the highest for a nearby contract since 1988.
"They've all been standing around the machines waiting for the export numbers to come out," one floor trader said.
The figure suggested to the market that USDA had underestimated export demand in Monday's monthly crop report. USDA left unchanged at 895 million bushels its forecast for U.S. soybean exports.
USDA also left its ending stocks figure at 125 million bushels but raised crush estimates by five million bushels.
At 1012 CDT, soymeal was up $3.10 to $0.70 per ton with July up $3.00 at $297.30 a ton.
Soybeans were up 5-3/4 to 1-3/4 cents per bushel with July up five at $8.94.
